title: Failure of a test from a module containing non-ASCII(?) characters results in SyntaxError when building AST for output

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: problem that needs to be addressed

body:
Originally reported by: **Chris Wood (BitBucket: [cpwood](http://bitbucket.org/cpwood), GitHub: [cpwood](http://github.com/cpwood))**

---

Example attached - runs ok from the command line with python 2.7 and py.test 2.3.5 and fails with the following when called with py.test:

```
#!python
============================= test session starts ==============================
platform linux2 -- Python 2.7.5 -- pytest-2.3.5
collected 1 items 

mytest.py F

=================================== FAILURES ===================================
___________________________________ test_me ____________________________________

source = 'True ==\nFalse\n    )', filename = '<unknown>', mode = 'exec'

    def parse(source, filename='<unknown>', mode='exec'):
        """
        Parse the source into an AST node.
        Equivalent to compile(source, filename, mode, PyCF_ONLY_AST).
        """
>       return compile(source, filename, mode, PyCF_ONLY_AST)
E         File "<unknown>", line 1
E           True ==
E                 ^
E       SyntaxError: invalid syntax

/usr/lib/python2.7/ast.py:37: SyntaxError
=========================== 1 failed in 0.02 seconds ===========================
```

The attached file contains this:

```
#!python
#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

BAD = u"–"

def test_me():
    assert(
        True ==
        False
    )

if __name__ == '__main__': test_me()

```
